# Revision plan: the box redesign and the road to M2

> **STATUS: PROPOSAL, written 2026-10-21 in Camden's session. Nothing in this file is a
> decision.** A decision exists only when it is recorded in `docs/DECISIONS.md` as
> ⚠️ UNREVIEWED, in the same commit as whatever enacts it, and signed later by a human.
> Claude never marks a decision reviewed or 🔒 LOCKED (`CLAUDE.md` §0).
>
> **Audience: a fresh Claude session with no memory of the conversation that produced this
> file.** Everything it needs is here or named by path. Where this file says "Camden
> decided", that is a statement about the 2026-10-21 conversation, and §1 says exactly
> which statements those are. Everything else is Claude's recommendation and must be
> confirmed with Camden before it is written down as settled.

## 0. How to use this file

1. Do the session-start steps in `CLAUDE.md` §0 first (read `docs/milestones.md`, the
   review queue at the top of `docs/DECISIONS.md`, run the board status, check `git
   status` is clean, `git pull`, create a branch **before** the first edit).
2. Read §1 (provenance), then §2 and §3 (the product and its engineering numbers), then
   §4 (what is wrong in the repo today).
3. Work through §8 in order. Each stage is one pull request; each commit inside it is one
   responsibility (`CLAUDE.md` §7.3). Do not skip ahead: later stages assume the earlier
   decisions exist.
4. Stop and ask Camden at every item in §11. Do not guess at them.
5. Obey §12 (the do-not list) at all times.
6. At the end of the session do the `CLAUDE.md` §0 end steps, including the transcript
   copy-out (`partners/camden/transcripts/README.md` now has the macOS command).

This plan edits documents first and code later. No money is spent by anything in it
(§10). Camden's standing instruction: be very sure of the paper plan before any part is
bought.

## 1. Provenance: what Camden decided, and what Claude only recommended

### 1.1 Decided by Camden in the 2026-10-21 conversation

| # | Statement |
| --- | --- |
| P1 | The team's 2008 Subaru Forester (non-turbo, Camden's car) is a testbed. Lance's 2015 Honda CR-V remains Lance's to use. **Neither car is required of anyone, and no document may restrict where either partner tests.** Camden's instruction, paraphrased: do not set limitations or restrictions for him, and especially not for Lance while the two of them are not communicating. |
| P2 | Tasks have no pre-assigned owners. Any open task is for whoever is available. For the handout's per-subsystem map, Camden chose **claim on first commit**: whoever lands a subsystem's first substantive commit is recorded as its owner. |
| P3 | The professor said the 48-hour soak means **48 hours of regular use** (not 48 hours powered): the car starts and stops, the product handles every cycle, is on and working every time the car runs, shuts down gracefully when the car shuts off, and auto-boots on the next start. Camden chose the reading "48 hours wall-clock of normal use". This has **not** been received in writing. |
| P4 | Camden approved **extending locked decision C.1** (append-only, CRC'd records) with write-ahead-log style transactions and checkpoints: a batch is `BEGIN`, records, `COMMIT`; recovery redoes committed work from the latest checkpoint and undoes uncommitted work. Camden's reason: it ties the project to the logging and checkpoint techniques taught in class. |
| P5 | `pisensor` (an MPU-6050 or similar on the Pi for mechanisms B and F) is **declined**. Mechanisms D and E stay the committed pair. |
| P6 | The Raspberry Pi 4 stays (both partners already own one). |
| P7 | **The product is one box.** The box has a single clean USB-C port (like a computer's) as its only power input. The user plugs in whatever USB-C charger and cable they already own. Camden: "no need to reinvent the charger." The team designs the box; the team buys only the OBD2 Bluetooth dongle and a cable. The box limits what any source can push, and supplements weak power from a small stored-energy element. |
| P8 | The stored-energy element is **small and short-lived by design**: its jobs are supplementing weak input power, bridging the dip at engine start, and giving the Pi enough time for a clean shutdown. It is **never** an always-on source and is not to be designed as one; about one minute of stored runtime is the ceiling and a few seconds to tens of seconds is the goal. The Pi is **intentionally off at rest**, which is what makes the 48-hour soak definition (P3) valid. |
| P9 | The Bluetooth OBD2 dongle is assumed to work as expected (Bluetooth Classic serial profile, **not BLE**). The box reads it, logs, and processes the data. |
| P10 | **Wake button: dropped.** The box has one port and one light and no buttons. |
| P11 | **One tri-color light.** Red means an issue, and "issue" means either a problem with the box or a problem with the car; the report says which. Yellow means starting or stopping on stored energy. Green means ready, all systems go. For pulse versus steady, Camden said whichever is safer, so §2.3 specifies pulsing. |
| P12 | The phone connects to the box (its own Wi-Fi) to view data and trends and to **download a report**. An app is "maybe": a stretch, not a commitment. |
| P13 | The box is "super small, sleek", with vents if needed. |
| P14 | **No shopping for now.** The paper plan comes first. |

### 1.2 Recommended by Claude, not confirmed by Camden (confirm before recording)

| # | Recommendation | Why it is still open |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1 | The stored-energy element is a **supercapacitor bank**, not a lithium cell. | Camden said "small rechargeable battery" first, then described the seconds-scale role. He never chose the chemistry. §3.1 has the reasoning (no thermal runaway, no charge-temperature cutoff to design, works in a hot or frozen car). |
| R2 | A **short grace period** after the source disappears, longer than a crank dip and shorter than the stored runtime, before shutdown starts. | Needs the Forester's real supply-dip measurement. |
| R3 | **Report as one HTML file plus a CSV**, served by a C program in `src/interface/`. | Camden said "report" and "maybe an app". Format is unchosen. |
| R4 | Steady yellow while booting (a not-yet-running state), pulses everywhere once alive. | See §2.3 and §11. |
| R5 | The phone page may set the Pi's clock (the Pi has no battery-backed clock). | Conflicts with D-013's "writes nothing". §11. |
| R6 | Record the Forester as the car the first baseline and fault captures run on. | Follows from P1 but is not itself a decision about Lance. |

### 1.3 Unknown, must be measured or asked

| # | Unknown | How to resolve |
| --- | --- | --- |
| U1 | Which Mode 01 PIDs the Forester answers, and its OBD protocol. A 2008 US car is expected to speak CAN (ISO 15765-4) but this is **not verified**. MAP may be absent. | PID survey (§8, stage 3). Do not assume; the sensor list and fault areas depend on it. |
| U2 | The Forester's supply behavior at crank, and whether its sockets and ports switch with the key. | Meter. Free first test: a USB charger with a light in the socket, key off. |
| U3 | Real Pi 4 boot and shutdown time and power draw on this image. | USB-C power meter and `systemd-analyze`. |
| U4 | The professor's written confirmation of the soak definition (P3). | Email, drafted in §9. Camden sends it. |
| U5 | Which deliverable is due "next Wednesday", 2026-10-28. The board has no such date: M2 was due 2026-10-11 and M3 is due 2026-11-01. | Camden checks the syllabus. |
| U6 | Whether Lance agrees with any of this. Lance has reviewed **no** decision in `docs/DECISIONS.md`. | Camden talks to Lance. Until then everything is ⚠️ UNREVIEWED. |

## 2. The product, as revised

### 2.1 In one paragraph

carwatch is a small plastic box with one USB-C port and one three-color light. It lives in
a car, plugged into whatever USB-C charger the owner already has. When the car powers
the charger the box boots, listens to the car's engine sensors through a Bluetooth OBD2
dongle, records everything to a crash-safe log, learns what *this car's* normal looks like
at each operating point, and flags behavior that leaves it, naming the likely fault area.
When the car shuts off, power disappears; the box notices, finishes its writes on a small
amount of stored energy, and halts cleanly, then sits off until the next start. A phone
joins the box's own Wi-Fi to see status and trends and to download a report that says
what is wrong with the box or the car. The claim we defend (D-021, to be reworded to "the
car it is installed in" by D-022): *it learns that car's normal across its Mode 01 engine
sensors, flags behavior outside it, and names the likely fault area, with measured catch
and false-alarm rates on faults we induce.* Not "predicts failure."

### 2.2 The physical product

| Item | Specification |
| --- | --- |
| Shell | Heat-resistant plastic (a cabin sits well above 60 °C parked in sun; ordinary PLA softens near 60 °C, so use ABS, ASA or similar, to be confirmed against the shell's datasheet). **No metal around the Pi's antenna**: Bluetooth and Wi-Fi share one radio. Vent slots on the top and bottom for passive airflow. Target envelope on the order of 95 × 65 × 30 mm for a Pi 4 plus the power board (estimate, to be confirmed against real parts). A food-container prototype is acceptable per the handout; the sleek shell is the product intent. |
| Power port | One USB-C receptacle. The only power input. Wired as a plain **sink** (5.1 kΩ resistors on both CC pins) so any source offers 5 V only. |
| Light | One tri-color LED visible through the shell. See §2.3. |
| Buttons | None. |
| Other ports | None. The OBD2 dongle is a separate item in the car's OBD2 port and reaches the box over Bluetooth, so no wire of ours touches it. |
| Install | Plug the dongle into the OBD2 port, plug the box into any USB-C charger in the car. Nothing is cut, spliced, pierced or clamped. |
| Inside | Raspberry Pi 4, microSD, a power block (§3.1), the light, and nothing else on the header. |
| Not supported | A power source that stays live with the key off. The box is designed for power that disappears when the car turns off; on an always-live port it would simply stay on. This is an installation requirement, written down as a limitation, not a mode to engineer around. |

### 2.3 The light

One tri-color LED on three GPIOs (each through its own resistor; value to be set by the
schematic against the chosen LED's datasheet). Written **only by the supervisor** (the
rule from D-014, kept).

| Color and pattern | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Green, slow pulse (about 1 Hz) | Ready: booted, recording, all systems go. |
| Yellow, medium blink (about 2 Hz) | Running on stored energy: starting up through a supply dip, or shutting down. |
| Red, fast blink (about 4 Hz) | An issue, in the box **or** the car. The report says which. |
| Steady any color, or dark while the car is on | The device is hung or not running. Never a valid live state. |
| Dark while the car is off | Normal. The box is powered down. |

Priority when more than one applies: red over yellow over green.

**Why every live state pulses.** A GPIO keeps its last level after the process that drove
it dies. A steady green would freeze into a false all-clear if the supervisor crashed. If
every live state blinks or pulses, a frozen light of any color can only mean "not
running." This is D-014's reasoning, applied to three colors. Camden said to choose
whichever is safer, and this is.

**Open (§11):** what the light shows during the roughly 20 to 40 seconds the Pi spends
booting, when no software can drive it yet. Recommendation R4: hold the yellow LED on in
hardware from power-up until the supervisor takes over the GPIOs, so *steady yellow* means
"booting, not yet running," consistent with the rule above.

**What counts as red** (the supervisor sets it; the report explains it):

- Box: a child process is down or restart-limited; the adapter has been silent while the
  engine is running; storage is failing or the disk is nearly full; undervoltage
  (`vcgencmd get_throttled` non-zero) or thermal throttling; the stored-energy element
  failed its self-check.
- Car: a verdict has surfaced after hysteresis and dwell (D.3): a fault
  area was named. A sensor the car stopped answering is also a car-side event.

### 2.4 What the box does in a drive (behavior, end to end)

1. The owner starts the car. The charger energizes. The box begins charging its stored
   energy and boots the Pi (light per §2.3).
2. `supervisor` starts `obdd`, `storaged`, `analyzed` and the status-page server, each
   supervised (mechanism E). A heartbeat appears within 60 seconds.
3. `obdd` finds the Bluetooth dongle at `/dev/obd`, initializes it, and round-robins Mode
   01 requests (D-012). Samples go through the shared-memory ring (B.3, refuse-don't-
   overwrite) to `storaged`, which writes them in committed batches (D-025).
4. `analyzed` bins by operating point, updates per-bin statistics, computes Mahalanobis
   residuals and Theil–Sen trends, classifies, and runs the state machine with hysteresis
   and dwell. Verdicts surface only after dwell.
5. The light goes green once everything is up.
6. The car turns off. Power disappears. The box detects it, waits out the grace period
   (R2), then: stops capture, commits the final batch, writes a checkpoint, syncs, and
   halts the Pi (light yellow). The power stage then removes the Pi's supply and the box
   is dark.
7. If anything goes wrong in step 6 (stored energy empty, cable pulled, source returns
   mid-shutdown), the crash-consistent log still recovers at the next boot (D-025). The
   clean shutdown is the normal path; crash consistency is the guarantee.
8. At the next start the cycle repeats and the box reports in its log whether the previous
   session ended cleanly or was recovered.

### 2.5 The phone

- The Pi runs its own Wi-Fi access point with WPA2, a per-device passphrase, and **no
  upstream and no internet** (D-013). The phone joins it. The product has no cloud.
- A read-only status page shows status, current verdicts and trends. A **Download report**
  button returns the report (R3). Nothing on the page can change the device, except the
  clock question in §11 (R5).
- A native app is a stretch and is not planned for M2 to M5. The page works on any phone.
- **The box is off when the car is off, so the phone can reach it only while the car
  is running or while the box is plugged into any charger at home.** This is a property
  of the product (P8), and it should be written in the README as a feature: plug it into
  a phone charger at home and it boots and serves the same page.
- `obdctl` remains the primary, exact interface with its five verbs (D-013 and the
  handout's "crisp CLI" guidance). Any graded behavior must be demonstrable through
  `obdctl` alone.

**Report contents (proposal, to be finalized in board item `reportspec`):**

| Section | Content |
| --- | --- |
| Header | Box id, report time, whether wall-clock time is trustworthy (the Pi has no battery-backed clock), `src` mix of the data (live, replay, synth: always labeled) |
| Sessions | Each key cycle: boot id, start, end, duration, ended cleanly or recovered, records lost on recovery |
| Box health | Process liveness and restarts, ring overruns (must be zero), undervoltage and throttle events, temperature, stored-energy self-check, storage free space |
| Car findings | Each surfaced verdict: fault area, which sensors cooperated to call it, residual and trend evidence, when it began and ended, confidence |
| Baseline maturity | Hours of normal driving learned per operating-point bin, so the owner knows how far to trust the verdicts |
| Absent signals | Any PID the car stopped answering, and for how long |

### 2.6 The 48-hour soak, under the professor's definition (P3)

Not 48 continuous powered hours. A **48-hour wall-clock window of normal use** in which:

- the box powers on at every key-on, records, and shuts down at every key-off;
- every drive shows a timestamped boot, hourly heartbeats while running (the Pi is off
  while parked, so the log shows deliberate gaps; this needs the professor's written okay,
  U4), and an orderly end of each session;
- **at least one injected fault** (unplug the OBD2 dongle for ten minutes while the engine
  is running, or `kill -9` a child) with detection, degradation and recovery visible;
- the key-off power loss counts as each session's end, and the log proves whether it was a
  clean shutdown or a recovery.

The raw logs are the deliverable and are never tidied (`soak/README.md`). Because the soak
now needs a real car, the fake OBD2 port (`obdsim`) is a development tool only, never the
soak's data source. Leave margin to run the soak twice.

## 3. Engineering specification

All numbers marked **(E)** are Claude's estimates from general knowledge, **not
measurements**, and must be replaced by measured values before they appear in
`docs/DESIGN.md` as anything but "estimate". `CLAUDE.md` §8.4: a measured voltage beats an
opinion.

### 3.1 The power block

```text
 any USB-C source ─▶ [CC sink, 5.1 kΩ x2] ─▶ [input protection] ─▶ [current limit,
                                                                    inrush control]
                                                                           │
                                  ┌────────────────────────────────────────┤
                                  ▼                                        ▼
                      [stored-energy element        [power-path: source first, stored
                       + balancing + fuse]  ◀──────  energy fills only the gap]
                                                                           │
                                                          [5 V, 3 A converter] ─▶ Pi 4
   "source present" ─▶ GPIO (shutdown trigger)        "halt done" ◀── GPIO (cut the converter)
```

**Requirements** (each becomes a line in `docs/hardware/wiring.md` with a measurement):

1. **Sink only, 5 V only.** A dumb sink never negotiates above 5 V, so no source can
   offer the Pi more than 5 V. Add transient and reverse-polarity protection and a fuse.
2. **Input current limit** below the source's rating, and an **inrush limiter**: an empty
   stored-energy element looks like a short circuit and would trip a modest source.
3. **Power-path behavior:** the source feeds the Pi first; the stored energy covers only
   the shortfall (weak source) or the gap (crank dip, source loss).
4. **Source-present signal** on a GPIO, so the supervisor can detect power loss.
5. **Halt-done signal:** when the Pi has finished halting, the power stage removes the
   converter output so the box goes fully dark and the stored energy is not wasted. The Pi
   can drive a GPIO low at poweroff (the `gpio-poweroff` device-tree overlay); confirm on
   the board.
6. **Auto power-on:** when the source returns, the converter must enable again without a
   button. This is how "auto boots on the next start" is satisfied.
7. **Stored energy bounded by design:** the element is sized so that stored runtime is
   on the order of tens of seconds and never approaches a minute at the Pi's load (P8).

**Sizing sketch (E, to be replaced by measurement):**

| Quantity | Estimate |
| --- | --- |
| Pi 4 draw during boot and shutdown | about 3 to 5 W |
| Clean-shutdown energy | 10 to 15 s × 4 W ÷ 0.85 converter efficiency ≈ 50 to 70 J |
| Crank-bridge energy | 1 to 3 s × 5 W ≈ 5 to 15 J |
| A bank of two series 2.7 V supercapacitor cells, 10 F total, charged to about 5 V | ½·C·V² ≈ 125 J stored, about 105 J usable above a 2 V converter floor |
| Charging time from empty at a 1 A budget | C·ΔV ÷ I ≈ 10 F × 5 V ÷ 1 A ≈ 50 s |

**Consequence the next session must not forget:** a 10 F bank needs on the order of a
minute to charge at 1 A. A smaller bank charges faster; a weaker source charges slower.
At a **cold start the bank is empty**, so it cannot bridge the crank dip on the first
start of a session, and the Pi may reset during cranking. That is survivable only because
of the crash-consistent log (D-025). The clean-shutdown path at key-off is reliable (the
bank has had a whole drive to charge); the crank-bridge path at key-on is best-effort and
must be described honestly in the design document. Measure it before claiming it.

**Why a supercapacitor (R1) rather than a lithium cell.** Lithium cells must not charge
above about 45 °C or below 0 °C, and a car cabin leaves that window on both ends (a
Colorado winter and a parked summer afternoon). Many cheap Pi UPS boards have no
temperature cutoff. A supercapacitor has no thermal-runaway failure mode, tolerates a wide
temperature range (confirm against the part's datasheet), and fits a seconds-scale job
exactly. Its costs are low voltage per cell (so two in series, with balancing), very low
internal resistance (so it needs a fuse), and a fast self-discharge that does not matter
for a box that is off at rest. If Camden prefers a cell anyway: use LiFePO4 or a charger
with a temperature-sense input that inhibits charging outside the safe window, a protected
cell, and a physical position away from the Pi's heat. Whichever is chosen, **a part
number goes into the BOM only with its datasheet linked and a human having checked it**
(`CLAUDE.md` §8.4; Claude cannot see the board).

**Mechanical and thermal:** a Pi 4 throttles near 80 °C. Cabin heat plus a sealed shell
is the likeliest way to hit that. Specify a heatsink, vents, and a measured temperature
in a hot parked car (board item `thermal`). Supercapacitor and SD-card temperature ratings
must cover the cabin's range.

### 3.2 Power-event state machine (the supervisor's, mechanism E)

| State | Entered when | The supervisor does | Light |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `BOOTING` | Linux up, supervisor starts | Starts children, waits for first heartbeats | steady yellow until it owns the GPIOs (R4), then yellow blink |
| `RUNNING` | All children healthy, source present | Normal operation | green pulse |
| `DEGRADED` | A child is down or restart-limited, adapter silent, storage or power fault | Keeps recording what it can, logs the distinction between absent and crashed | red blink |
| `GRACE` | Source-present signal lost | Starts a timer. Keeps recording. If the source returns, return to `RUNNING` | yellow blink |
| `SHUTTING_DOWN` | Grace timer expired with no source | Stops `obdd`, tells `storaged` to commit and checkpoint, `sync`, `shutdown -h` | yellow blink |
| `OFF` | Pi halted, converter cut | Nothing runs | dark |

Open edge cases to settle in `shutfsm` before any code: the grace period's length (longer
than a crank dip, shorter than the stored runtime); what happens if the source returns
mid-`SHUTTING_DOWN` (recommended: finish the clean shutdown, then let the box reboot,
which is safe if annoying); a false trigger from a supply dip while running; and what the
supervisor does when the stored-energy self-check fails.

### 3.3 Storage: write-ahead transactions and checkpoints (mechanism D, D-025)

This extends 🔒 C.1; it does not remove any of its rules. Records stay append-only,
self-framing (magic), and CRC'd over the whole record, and every record keeps its `src`
tag (C.2).

- **Transaction.** `storaged` drains the ring into a batch: `BEGIN(txn_id)`, the sample
  records, `COMMIT(txn_id)`, then one `fsync`. A batch is durable only once its `COMMIT`
  is on disk.
- **Checkpoint.** Periodically (rarely, to keep the write load and memory low), write a
  snapshot of the learned baselines plus the log offset and last committed `txn_id` it
  covers. Use **two alternating slots (A/B)**, each CRC'd and carrying a generation
  counter, so a checkpoint torn by a power cut can never destroy the previous good one.
- **Recovery at boot.** Load the newest valid checkpoint. Scan the log forward from its
  offset, verifying every CRC. **Redo**: re-apply every committed transaction to the
  baselines. **Undo**: any transaction with no `COMMIT` is truncated at its `BEGIN`; the
  scan stops at the first bad CRC and truncates the torn tail. Log exactly what was
  recovered and what was lost (counts and offsets).
- **Why undo is only truncation.** Nothing is ever overwritten in place (that is C.1's
  point), so there is no before-image to restore. State this plainly in the design
  document and at the defense; do not claim an undo log the design does not need.
- **Record format proposal (decision `recfmt`, to be confirmed):** add kinds
  `REC_TXN_BEGIN`, `REC_TXN_COMMIT`, `REC_CHECKPOINT` and `REC_BOOT` to `rec_kind_t` in
  `include/store/record.h`; add a `boot_id` to the header (there is a spare 16-bit field
  today; a 32-bit `boot_id` needs a layout change, so bump `REC_VERSION` to 2 and keep the
  known-answer CRC test unchanged); every session starts with a `REC_BOOT` record that
  states whether the previous session ended cleanly.
- **fsync policy (provisional, `fsync`):** one commit and one `fsync` per batch of about
  one second. Records are about 48 bytes (a 40-byte header plus a small payload, E), the
  request budget is about 10 to 20 per second (D-012), so about 1 KB/s, about 3.5 MB per
  hour of running, and on the order of 170 MB over 48 *running* hours (the 48 hour
  *wall-clock* soak records far less because the box is off while parked). The worst loss
  from a power cut that beats the clean shutdown is about one second of samples, which
  holds nothing a user would miss. The argument for the batch size must be written in
  `docs/DESIGN.md` §4 before the code is written (C.1's standing instruction).
- **Baseline persistence:** learned per-bin statistics are the model's state, so they must
  survive every key cycle. Checkpoint plus replay since the checkpoint is exactly how.
- **Clock:** the Pi has no battery-backed clock. Every record carries `mono_ns` and a
  `boot_id`; wall time is best-effort. Raspberry Pi OS ships `fake-hwclock`, which saves
  the time at a clean shutdown and restores it at boot, so a clean shutdown also keeps the
  clock close. Verify on the image.

### 3.4 The boot-time budget

A stock Pi 4 takes roughly 25 to 40 seconds to boot (E), and Camden's "a few seconds" is
not achievable without a trimmed image. The Forester's cooling warm-up is the most
informative part of a drive, so a lost first half-minute is a real cost: the design
document's substitutions section must say so. Mitigations to measure (board items
`bootbudget`, `bootimg`): disable unused services, `systemd-analyze blame`, start `obdd`
as early as possible, and let capture begin before the phone Wi-Fi is up.

### 3.5 Failure-mode rows to add or change in `docs/DESIGN.md` §3

New rows for the redesign (each needs Detection, Response, and a *real* log line, filled
in when the code exists):

| Component | Failure | Detection | Response |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Power | Source disappears (normal key-off) | source-present GPIO | grace, clean shutdown (§3.2) |
| Power | Source dips at crank | source-present glitch shorter than the grace period | ride through; log the dip |
| Power | Source returns mid-shutdown | source-present rises during `SHUTTING_DOWN` | finish shutdown, reboot |
| Power | Stored energy empty at key-off (bank not charged, weak source) | self-check or failed shutdown timing | crash-consistent recovery next boot (D-025) |
| Power | Charger yanked mid-drive | same as key-off | same as key-off, logged as unplanned |
| Power | Weak source (undervoltage) | `vcgencmd get_throttled` | red; log; the stored energy supplements |
| Thermal | Pi throttles in a hot cabin | `vcgencmd get_throttled`, temperature | red; log; report shows it |
| Storage | SD card fails or fills | write error, free-space check | degrade and log; do not crash |
| Radio | Bluetooth and Wi-Fi contend | `btcoex` measurement | measure and document |

76	## 2. The product, as revised
77	
78	### 2.1 In one paragraph
79	
80	carwatch is a small plastic box with one USB-C port and one three-color light. It lives in
81	a car, plugged into whatever USB-C charger the owner already has. When the car powers
82	the charger the box boots, listens to the car's engine sensors through a Bluetooth OBD2
83	dongle, records everything to a crash-safe log, learns what *this car's* normal looks like
84	at each operating point, and flags behavior that leaves it, naming the likely fault area.
85	When the car shuts off, power disappears; the box notices, finishes its writes on a small
86	amount of stored energy, and halts cleanly, then sits off until the next start. A phone
87	joins the box's own Wi-Fi to see status and trends and to download a report that says
88	what is wrong with the box or the car. The claim we defend (D-021, to be reworded to "the
89	car it is installed in" by D-022): *it learns that car's normal across its Mode 01 engine
90	sensors, flags behavior outside it, and names the likely fault area, with measured catch
91	and false-alarm rates on faults we induce.* Not "predicts failure."
92	
93	### 2.2 The physical product
94	
95	| Item | Specification |
96	| --- | --- |
97	| Shell | Heat-resistant plastic (a cabin sits well above 60 °C parked in sun; ordinary PLA softens near 60 °C, so use ABS, ASA or similar, to be confirmed against the shell's datasheet). **No metal around the Pi's antenna**: Bluetooth and Wi-Fi share one radio. Vent slots on the top and bottom for passive airflow. Target envelope on the order of 95 × 65 × 30 mm for a Pi 4 plus the power board (estimate, to be confirmed against real parts). A food-container prototype is acceptable per the handout; the sleek shell is the product intent. |
98	| Power port | One USB-C receptacle. The only power input. Wired as a plain **sink** (5.1 kΩ resistors on both CC pins) so any source offers 5 V only. |
99	| Light | One tri-color LED visible through the shell. See §2.3. |
100	| Buttons | None. |
101	| Other ports | None. The OBD2 dongle is a separate item in the car's OBD2 port and reaches the box over Bluetooth, so no wire of ours touches it. |
102	| Install | Plug the dongle into the OBD2 port, plug the box into any USB-C charger in the car. Nothing is cut, spliced, pierced or clamped. |
103	| Inside | Raspberry Pi 4, microSD, a power block (§3.1), the light, and nothing else on the header. |
104	| Not supported | A power source that stays live with the key off. The box is designed for power that disappears when the car turns off; on an always-live port it would simply stay on. This is an installation requirement, written down as a limitation, not a mode to engineer around. |
105	
106	### 2.3 The light
107	
108	One tri-color LED on three GPIOs (each through its own resistor; value to be set by the
109	schematic against the chosen LED's datasheet). Written **only by the supervisor** (the
110	rule from D-014, kept).
111	
112	| Color and pattern | Meaning |
113	| --- | --- |
114	| Green, slow pulse (about 1 Hz) | Ready: booted, recording, all systems go. |
115	| Yellow, medium blink (about 2 Hz) | Running on stored energy: starting up through a supply dip, or shutting down. |
116	| Red, fast blink (about 4 Hz) | An issue, in the box **or** the car. The report says which. |
117	| Steady any color, or dark while the car is on | The device is hung or not running. Never a valid live state. |
118	| Dark while the car is off | Normal. The box is powered down. |
119	
120	Priority when more than one applies: red over yellow over green.
121	
122	**Why every live state pulses.** A GPIO keeps its last level after the process that drove
123	it dies. A steady green would freeze into a false all-clear if the supervisor crashed. If
124	every live state blinks or pulses, a frozen light of any color can only mean "not
125	running." This is D-014's reasoning, applied to three colors. Camden said to choose
126	whichever is safer, and this is.
127	
128	**Open (§11):** what the light shows during the roughly 20 to 40 seconds the Pi spends
129	booting, when no software can drive it yet. Recommendation R4: hold the yellow LED on in
130	hardware from power-up until the supervisor takes over the GPIOs, so *steady yellow* means
131	"booting, not yet running," consistent with the rule above.
132	
133	**What counts as red** (the supervisor sets it; the report explains it):
134	
135	- Box: a child process is down or restart-limited; the adapter has been silent while the
136	  engine is running; storage is failing or the disk is nearly full; undervoltage
137	  (`vcgencmd get_throttled` non-zero) or thermal throttling; the stored-energy element
138	  failed its self-check.
139	- Car: a verdict has surfaced after hysteresis and dwell (D.3): a fault
140	  area was named. A sensor the car stopped answering is also a car-side event.
141	
142	### 2.4 What the box does in a drive (behavior, end to end)
143	
144	1. The owner starts the car. The charger energizes. The box begins charging its stored
145	   energy and boots the Pi (light per §2.3).
146	2. `supervisor` starts `obdd`, `storaged`, `analyzed` and the status-page server, each
147	   supervised (mechanism E). A heartbeat appears within 60 seconds.
148	3. `obdd` finds the Bluetooth dongle at `/dev/obd`, initializes it, and round-robins Mode
149	   01 requests (D-012). Samples go through the shared-memory ring (B.3, refuse-don't-
150	   overwrite) to `storaged`, which writes them in committed batches (D-025).
151	4. `analyzed` bins by operating point, updates per-bin statistics, computes Mahalanobis
152	   residuals and Theil–Sen trends, classifies, and runs the state machine with hysteresis
153	   and dwell. Verdicts surface only after dwell.
154	5. The light goes green once everything is up.
155	6. The car turns off. Power disappears. The box detects it, waits out the grace period
156	   (R2), then: stops capture, commits the final batch, writes a checkpoint, syncs, and
157	   halts the Pi (light yellow). The power stage then removes the Pi's supply and the box
158	   is dark.
159	7. If anything goes wrong in step 6 (stored energy empty, cable pulled, source returns
160	   mid-shutdown), the crash-consistent log still recovers at the next boot (D-025). The
161	   clean shutdown is the normal path; crash consistency is the guarantee.
162	8. At the next start the cycle repeats and the box reports in its log whether the previous
163	   session ended cleanly or was recovered.
164	
165	### 2.5 The phone
166	
167	- The Pi runs its own Wi-Fi access point with WPA2, a per-device passphrase, and **no
168	  upstream and no internet** (D-013). The phone joins it. The product has no cloud.
169	- A read-only status page shows status, current verdicts and trends. A **Download report**
170	  button returns the report (R3). Nothing on the page can change the device, except the
171	  clock question in §11 (R5).
172	- A native app is a stretch and is not planned for M2 to M5. The page works on any phone.
173	- **The box is off when the car is off, so the phone can reach it only while the car
174	  is running or while the box is plugged into any charger at home.** This is a property
175	  of the product (P8), and it should be written in the README as a feature: plug it into
176	  a phone charger at home and it boots and serves the same page.
177	- `obdctl` remains the primary, exact interface with its five verbs (D-013 and the
178	  handout's "crisp CLI" guidance). Any graded behavior must be demonstrable through
179	  `obdctl` alone.
180	
181	**Report contents (proposal, to be finalized in board item `reportspec`):**
182	
183	| Section | Content |
184	| --- | --- |
185	| Header | Box id, report time, whether wall-clock time is trustworthy (the Pi has no battery-backed clock), `src` mix of the data (live, replay, synth: always labeled) |
186	| Sessions | Each key cycle: boot id, start, end, duration, ended cleanly or recovered, records lost on recovery |
187	| Box health | Process liveness and restarts, ring overruns (must be zero), undervoltage and throttle events, temperature, stored-energy self-check, storage free space |
188	| Car findings | Each surfaced verdict: fault area, which sensors cooperated to call it, residual and trend evidence, when it began and ended, confidence |
189	| Baseline maturity | Hours of normal driving learned per operating-point bin, so the owner knows how far to trust the verdicts |
190	| Absent signals | Any PID the car stopped answering, and for how long |
191	
192	### 2.6 The 48-hour soak, under the professor's definition (P3)
193	
194	Not 48 continuous powered hours. A **48-hour wall-clock window of normal use** in which:
195	
196	- the box powers on at every key-on, records, and shuts down at every key-off;
197	- every drive shows a timestamped boot, hourly heartbeats while running (the Pi is off
198	  while parked, so the log shows deliberate gaps; this needs the professor's written okay,
199	  U4), and an orderly end of each session;
200	- **at least one injected fault** (unplug the OBD2 dongle for ten minutes while the engine
201	  is running, or `kill -9` a child) with detection, degradation and recovery visible;
202	- the key-off power loss counts as each session's end, and the log proves whether it was a
203	  clean shutdown or a recovery.
204	
205	The raw logs are the deliverable and are never tidied (`soak/README.md`). Because the soak
206	now needs a real car, the fake OBD2 port (`obdsim`) is a development tool only, never the
207	soak's data source. Leave margin to run the soak twice.
208	
209	## 3. Engineering specification
210	
211	All numbers marked **(E)** are Claude's estimates from general knowledge, **not
212	measurements**, and must be replaced by measured values before they appear in
213	`docs/DESIGN.md` as anything but "estimate". `CLAUDE.md` §8.4: a measured voltage beats an
214	opinion.
215	
216	### 3.1 The power block
217	
218	```text
219	 any USB-C source ─▶ [CC sink, 5.1 kΩ x2] ─▶ [input protection] ─▶ [current limit,
220	                                                                    inrush control]
221	                                                                           │
222	                                  ┌────────────────────────────────────────┤
223	                                  ▼                                        ▼
224	                      [stored-energy element        [power-path: source first, stored
225	                       + balancing + fuse]  ◀──────  energy fills only the gap]
226	                                                                           │
227	                                                          [5 V, 3 A converter] ─▶ Pi 4
228	   "source present" ─▶ GPIO (shutdown trigger)        "halt done" ◀── GPIO (cut the converter)
229	```
230	
231	**Requirements** (each becomes a line in `docs/hardware/wiring.md` with a measurement):
232	
233	1. **Sink only, 5 V only.** A dumb sink never negotiates above 5 V, so no source can
234	   offer the Pi more than 5 V. Add transient and reverse-polarity protection and a fuse.
235	2. **Input current limit** below the source's rating, and an **inrush limiter**: an empty
236	   stored-energy element looks like a short circuit and would trip a modest source.
237	3. **Power-path behavior:** the source feeds the Pi first; the stored energy covers only
238	   the shortfall (weak source) or the gap (crank dip, source loss).
239	4. **Source-present signal** on a GPIO, so the supervisor can detect power loss.
240	5. **Halt-done signal:** when the Pi has finished halting, the power stage removes the
241	   converter output so the box goes fully dark and the stored energy is not wasted. The Pi
242	   can drive a GPIO low at poweroff (the `gpio-poweroff` device-tree overlay); confirm on
243	   the board.
244	6. **Auto power-on:** when the source returns, the converter must enable again without a
245	   button. This is how "auto boots on the next start" is satisfied.
246	7. **Stored energy bounded by design:** the element is sized so that stored runtime is
247	   on the order of tens of seconds and never approaches a minute at the Pi's load (P8).
248	
249	**Sizing sketch (E, to be replaced by measurement):**
250	
251	| Quantity | Estimate |
252	| --- | --- |
253	| Pi 4 draw during boot and shutdown | about 3 to 5 W |
254	| Clean-shutdown energy | 10 to 15 s × 4 W ÷ 0.85 converter efficiency ≈ 50 to 70 J |
255	| Crank-bridge energy | 1 to 3 s × 5 W ≈ 5 to 15 J |
256	| A bank of two series 2.7 V supercapacitor cells, 10 F total, charged to about 5 V | ½·C·V² ≈ 125 J stored, about 105 J usable above a 2 V converter floor |
257	| Charging time from empty at a 1 A budget | C·ΔV ÷ I ≈ 10 F × 5 V ÷ 1 A ≈ 50 s |
258	
259	**Consequence the next session must not forget:** a 10 F bank needs on the order of a
260	minute to charge at 1 A. A smaller bank charges faster; a weaker source charges slower.
261	At a **cold start the bank is empty**, so it cannot bridge the crank dip on the first
262	start of a session, and the Pi may reset during cranking. That is survivable only because
263	of the crash-consistent log (D-025). The clean-shutdown path at key-off is reliable (the
264	bank has had a whole drive to charge); the crank-bridge path at key-on is best-effort and
265	must be described honestly in the design document. Measure it before claiming it.
266	
267	**Why a supercapacitor (R1) rather than a lithium cell.** Lithium cells must not charge
268	above about 45 °C or below 0 °C, and a car cabin leaves that window on both ends (a
269	Colorado winter and a parked summer afternoon). Many cheap Pi UPS boards have no
270	temperature cutoff. A supercapacitor has no thermal-runaway failure mode, tolerates a wide
271	temperature range (confirm against the part's datasheet), and fits a seconds-scale job
272	exactly. Its costs are low voltage per cell (so two in series, with balancing), very low
273	internal resistance (so it needs a fuse), and a fast self-discharge that does not matter
274	for a box that is off at rest. If Camden prefers a cell anyway: use LiFePO4 or a charger
275	with a temperature-sense input that inhibits charging outside the safe window, a protected
276	cell, and a physical position away from the Pi's heat. Whichever is chosen, **a part
277	number goes into the BOM only with its datasheet linked and a human having checked it**
278	(`CLAUDE.md` §8.4; Claude cannot see the board).
279	
280	**Mechanical and thermal:** a Pi 4 throttles near 80 °C. Cabin heat plus a sealed shell
281	is the likeliest way to hit that. Specify a heatsink, vents, and a measured temperature
282	in a hot parked car (board item `thermal`). Supercapacitor and SD-card temperature ratings
283	must cover the cabin's range.

285	### 3.2 Power-event state machine (the supervisor's, mechanism E)
286	
287	| State | Entered when | The supervisor does | Light |
288	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
289	| `BOOTING` | Linux up, supervisor starts | Starts children, waits for first heartbeats | steady yellow until it owns the GPIOs (R4), then yellow blink |
290	| `RUNNING` | All children healthy, source present | Normal operation | green pulse |
291	| `DEGRADED` | A child is down or restart-limited, adapter silent, storage or power fault | Keeps recording what it can, logs the distinction between absent and crashed | red blink |
292	| `GRACE` | Source-present signal lost | Starts a timer. Keeps recording. If the source returns, return to `RUNNING` | yellow blink |
293	| `SHUTTING_DOWN` | Grace timer expired with no source | Stops `obdd`, tells `storaged` to commit and checkpoint, `sync`, `shutdown -h` | yellow blink |
294	| `OFF` | Pi halted, converter cut | Nothing runs | dark |
295	
296	Open edge cases to settle in `shutfsm` before any code: the grace period's length (longer
297	than a crank dip, shorter than the stored runtime); what happens if the source returns
298	mid-`SHUTTING_DOWN` (recommended: finish the clean shutdown, then let the box reboot,
299	which is safe if annoying); a false trigger from a supply dip while running; and what the
300	supervisor does when the stored-energy self-check fails.

302	### 3.3 Storage: write-ahead transactions and checkpoints (mechanism D, D-025)
303	
304	This extends 🔒 C.1; it does not remove any of its rules. Records stay append-only,
305	self-framing (magic), and CRC'd over the whole record, and every record keeps its `src`
306	tag (C.2).
307	
308	- **Transaction.** `storaged` drains the ring into a batch: `BEGIN(txn_id)`, the sample
309	  records, `COMMIT(txn_id)`, then one `fsync`. A batch is durable only once its `COMMIT`
310	  is on disk.
311	- **Checkpoint.** Periodically (rarely, to keep the write load and memory low), write a
312	  snapshot of the learned baselines plus the log offset and last committed `txn_id` it
313	  covers. Use **two alternating slots (A/B)**, each CRC'd and carrying a generation
314	  counter, so a checkpoint torn by a power cut can never destroy the previous good one.
315	- **Recovery at boot.** Load the newest valid checkpoint. Scan the log forward from its
316	  offset, verifying every CRC. **Redo**: re-apply every committed transaction to the
317	  baselines. **Undo**: any transaction with no `COMMIT` is truncated at its `BEGIN`; the
318	  scan stops at the first bad CRC and truncates the torn tail. Log exactly what was
319	  recovered and what was lost (counts and offsets).
320	- **Why undo is only truncation.** Nothing is ever overwritten in place (that is C.1's
321	  point), so there is no before-image to restore. State this plainly in the design
322	  document and at the defense; do not claim an undo log the design does not need.
323	- **Record format proposal (decision `recfmt`, to be confirmed):** add kinds
324	  `REC_TXN_BEGIN`, `REC_TXN_COMMIT`, `REC_CHECKPOINT` and `REC_BOOT` to `rec_kind_t` in
325	  `include/store/record.h`; add a `boot_id` to the header (there is a spare 16-bit field
326	  today; a 32-bit `boot_id` needs a layout change, so bump `REC_VERSION` to 2 and keep the
327	  known-answer CRC test unchanged); every session starts with a `REC_BOOT` record that
328	  states whether the previous session ended cleanly.
329	- **fsync policy (provisional, `fsync`):** one commit and one `fsync` per batch of about
330	  one second. Records are about 48 bytes (a 40-byte header plus a small payload, E), the
331	  request budget is about 10 to 20 per second (D-012), so about 1 KB/s, about 3.5 MB per
332	  hour of running, and on the order of 170 MB over 48 *running* hours (the 48 hour
333	  *wall-clock* soak records far less because the box is off while parked). The worst loss
334	  from a power cut that beats the clean shutdown is about one second of samples, which
335	  holds nothing a user would miss. The argument for the batch size must be written in
336	  `docs/DESIGN.md` §4 before the code is written (C.1's standing instruction).
337	- **Baseline persistence:** learned per-bin statistics are the model's state, so they must
338	  survive every key cycle. Checkpoint plus replay since the checkpoint is exactly how.
339	- **Clock:** the Pi has no battery-backed clock. Every record carries `mono_ns` and a
340	  `boot_id`; wall time is best-effort. Raspberry Pi OS ships `fake-hwclock`, which saves
341	  the time at a clean shutdown and restores it at boot, so a clean shutdown also keeps the
342	  clock close. Verify on the image.
343	
344	### 3.4 The boot-time budget
345	
346	A stock Pi 4 takes roughly 25 to 40 seconds to boot (E), and Camden's "a few seconds" is
347	not achievable without a trimmed image. The Forester's cooling warm-up is the most
348	informative part of a drive, so a lost first half-minute is a real cost: the design
349	document's substitutions section must say so. Mitigations to measure (board items
350	`bootbudget`, `bootimg`): disable unused services, `systemd-analyze blame`, start `obdd`
351	as early as possible, and let capture begin before the phone Wi-Fi is up.

282	## B. Systems architecture and mechanisms
283	
284	### B.1 — Mechanism commitments: D and E; B and F only with a Pi-side sensor ⚠️ UNREVIEWED
285	
286	`D-017` · Decided M1, 2026-09-21 · **By:** Camden + Claude
287	· **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜
288	· **Supersedes:** D-002 (§G.3)
289	
290	The handout requires two, implemented by us and measured.
291	
292	| Mechanism | Status | Where |
293	| --- | --- | --- |
294	| **D** — custom append-only storage, crash-consistent | **committed** | `src/store/` |
295	| **E** — multi-process with a supervisor | **committed** | `src/supervisor/`, `src/ipc/` |
296	| **B** — interrupt-driven input with a polling comparison | only if `pisensor` adds an MPU-6050 | capture path for that sensor |
297	| **F** — high-rate no-drop SPSC ring | only if `pisensor` adds an MPU-6050 | `src/ipc/ring.c` |
298	| **A**, **C**, raw CAN | stretch, after D and E are measured | — |
299	
300	**D.** *The defining constraint: power is cut mid-write every time the key turns off*
301	(D-011). We never get a clean shutdown. Measured by pulling power mid-write, repeatedly,
302	and proving recovery (`expcrash`).
303	
304	**E.** A recorder that dies silently has actively harmed its user, who believes it is on
305	duty. Any child may be `kill -9`'d; the system degrades, logs, recovers. Measured by killing
306	each child repeatedly and timing detection and recovery (`expkill`).
307	
308	**Why B and F left the OBD data path (D-015, D-019).** B needs an interrupt that *our*
309	design services. The adapter's interrupts belong to the kernel's Bluetooth and RFCOMM
310	stack; our process only blocks on a tty, and at ~10–20 replies/s a poll loop keeps up
311	trivially — the comparison would measure the tty layer, not a design of ours. F needs a
312	*high-rate* stream; ~10–20 samples/s never stresses a ring, so "zero drops under
313	contention" would be true and meaningless.
314	
315	**What brings them back.** An MPU-6050 on the Pi's I2C, its `INT` pin on a GPIO: kHz
316	samples from a hardware FIFO give a real interrupt-vs-polling comparison (B) and a rate
317	that stresses the ring (F). That is board item `pisensor`, due at M2.
318	
319	**The ring stays regardless.** It is how capture hands samples to storage across the
320	process boundary E requires, and B.3 still binds it.
321	
322	**Risk.** D and E alone meet the floor exactly. If either measurement fails, nothing is in
323	reserve — which is why `pisensor` is on the critical path.
324	
325	### B.2 — Four processes, not one 🔒
326	
327	`D-002` (corollary) · **By:** Camden + Claude · **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜
328	
329	`obdd`, `storaged`, `analyzed` and `supervisor` are separate processes with separate
330	address spaces, communicating over a shared-memory ring and Unix domain sockets.
331	
332	**Why.** Fault isolation is the product requirement, not an architectural preference: the
333	analysis engine is the most complex and least trustworthy component, and it must not be
334	able to take the capture path down with it. One process would be simpler and would fail
335	the thing the device exists to do.
336	
337	### B.3 — The ring refuses rather than overwrites 🔒
338	
339	Decided M0 · **By:** Claude, from D-002 · **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜
340	
341	When the ring is full the producer returns failure and increments an overrun counter. It
342	does **not** overwrite the oldest unread slot.
343	
344	**Why.** Overwriting loses data silently, and silent loss is the exact failure mechanism F
345	exists to make impossible. A refusal is visible, countable, and reportable; an overwrite
346	looks like a quiet minute. Enforced by `tests/test_ring.c`.
347	
348	**Reviewer note.** This is a real trade: under sustained overload we drop *new* data
349	rather than *old*. If that is ever the wrong choice for a diagnostic, reopen this.

388	### B.5 — One warning light, driven by the supervisor ⚠️ UNREVIEWED
389	
390	`D-014` · Decided M1, 2026-09-21 · **By:** Camden + Claude
391	· **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜
392	
393	**Decision.** One LED on a GPIO (proposed GPIO17, header pin 11, through 330 Ω), written
394	**only by the supervisor**. Every state in which the device is working is a *blink
395	pattern*:
396	
397	| Light | Meaning | Priority |
398	| --- | --- | --- |
399	| fast blink (~4 Hz) | **degraded** — a child is down, the adapter silent while the engine runs, storage failing, or undervoltage | highest |
400	| double-blink, pause | **a verdict has surfaced** (after D.3 hysteresis and dwell) — look at the phone | |
401	| slow blink (~1 Hz) | on duty, recording, nothing to report | lowest |
402	| **steady on or steady off** | **the device is not running.** Never a valid state. | — |
403	
404	**Why a light at all.** The 3 a.m. test: nobody is looking at a phone at the moment that
405	matters. It also makes "honest reporting through our own interface" (demo movement 1)
406	visible from across the room when a sensor is unplugged.
407	
408	**Why every live state blinks.** A GPIO keeps its last level after the process driving it
409	dies. If "verdict" were solid-on, a crashed supervisor would freeze the light into a false
410	alarm, or into a false all-clear if it froze off. With blink-only states, a stuck light of
411	either kind can only mean *not running*. This is mechanism E's principle — a recorder that
412	dies silently has harmed its user — applied to the one output a driver actually sees.
413	
414	**Why the supervisor, not `analyzed`.** The supervisor already knows every child's
415	liveness (mechanism E), so it can show "degraded" when `analyzed` itself has died; a light
416	owned by `analyzed` would show a stale verdict instead. Verdicts reach the supervisor over
417	the existing UDS. One writer, no GPIO contention.
418	
419	**Cost.** One more thing the supervisor does, and one more thing it must not block on: the
420	blink timer must never delay `waitpid` handling. Color, brightness and placement are open
421	(M4 enclosure).

425	## C. Storage and data integrity
426	
427	### C.1 — Append-only, self-framing, CRC'd records 🔒
428	
429	`D-002/D` · Decided M0 · **By:** Camden + Claude · **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜
430	
431	Records are never rewritten in place. Each carries a magic number for resynchronization
432	and a CRC32 over its whole body. Recovery scans from the last known-good offset, verifies
433	CRCs, truncates the torn tail, and logs exactly what was lost.
434	
435	**Why.** We are interrupted mid-write by design, several times a day. Rewriting in place
436	can destroy data that was previously correct; appending can only ever damage the last
437	record. The CRC is what makes a torn record *detectable* rather than merely wrong — and
438	wrong numbers you trust are more dangerous than missing numbers you know about.
439	
440	**Open sub-decision (M2, Lance):** fsync batch size and interval. There is no correct
441	value, only one justifiable from user requirements. Document the argument in `docs/DESIGN.md`
442	§4 before writing the code.
443	
444	### C.2 — Every record carries a provenance tag 🔒
445	
446	Decided M0 · **By:** Camden + Claude · **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜
447	
448	Every record and every log line carries `src = live | replay | synth`. Present in the
449	format from day one, before any replay tooling exists.
450	
451	**Why.** Handout §5: replayed or synthesized data must be labeled everywhere it appears —
452	logs, report, demo. Making it a mandatory field rather than a convention means it is
453	structurally impossible to forget. Mislabeling synthesized data as live is the single
454	integrity failure this course is best equipped to detect, and the worst trade available
455	anywhere in it.

459	## D. Intelligence and analysis
460	
461	### D.1 — Self-trained model; training in Python, inference in C 🔒
462	
463	`D-004` · Decided M0 · **By:** Camden (confirmed with instructor)
464	· **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜
465	
466	A locally-trained, self-authored model is permitted; hosted APIs and third-party
467	pretrained weights are not. Therefore: training in `tools/train/`, weights versioned under
468	`models/` with the training commit in the header, **inference in C in `src/analysis/`**, no
469	network at runtime.
470	
471	**Why inference in C.** First and most important for the grade: the runtime path sits
472	inside the supervised multi-process architecture, and a Python process there muddies the
473	boundary a grader must verify in sixty seconds. Second: it removes an interpreter, a
474	garbage collector and ~30 MB of RSS from a 48-hour memory-stability test we are graded on.
475	
476	**What the model is not doing.** The features are the intelligence — operating-point
477	binning, per-bin baselines, Mahalanobis residuals, Theil–Sen trends, all hand-written.
478	Delete the weights file and the system still produces residuals and trends; it loses only
479	the final labeling step. That separation is deliberate and it is the answer at the defense.
480	
481	### D.2 — Analysis pipeline shape 🔒
482	
483	Decided M0 · **By:** Camden + Claude · **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜
484	
485	Operating-point binning (RPM × load × coolant temp) → per-bin running mean/variance →
486	multivariate residual (Mahalanobis) → robust trend (Theil–Sen) → classifier → state
487	machine with hysteresis and dwell.
488	
489	**Why binning comes first.** Comparing a cold idle to a warm cruise is a false-alarm
490	generator. Every comparison happens inside one bin, against genuinely comparable
491	conditions. This single step removes more false positives than anything else downstream.
492	
493	**Why multivariate.** The signal is the *correlation between sensors*, not any single
494	sensor's value — oil pressure is supposed to rise with RPM. A measure of anomaly that
495	already accounts for normal partnerships, and alarms only when a partnership breaks, is
496	what makes this something a threshold provably cannot do (handout §3.3).
497	
498	### D.3 — Hysteresis and dwell before any verdict surfaces 🔒
499	
500	Decided M0 · **By:** Camden + Claude · **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜
501	
502	No verdict reaches the user until it has persisted. Trip and un-trip levels differ
503	deliberately.
504	
505	**Why.** A monitor that cries wolf twice gets unplugged, and an unplugged monitor is worse
506	than none because someone far away believes it is on duty. **False-positive rate is a
507	first-class metric in `docs/EVALUATION.md`, not an afterthought.**
508	
509	### D.4 — The threshold test, as a standing rule 🔒
510	
511	Decided M0 · **By:** Camden + Claude · **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜
512	
513	Every diagnostic we ship must require at least two cooperating sensors to reach its
514	conclusion. If a single threshold on a single value could produce the verdict, it is not
515	intelligence and it does not count. **Write the reason down in `docs/DESIGN.md` when
516	adding a diagnostic** — this is checked at the defense.

522	### E.1 — A one-car monitor that learns normal and names the fault area ⚠️ UNREVIEWED
523	
524	`D-021` · Decided M1, 2026-09-23 · **By:** Camden, reopening 🔒 D-003 in session, + Claude
525	· **Reviewed:** Camden ⬜ / Lance ⬜ · **Supersedes:** D-003 (§G.5)
526	
527	**Decision.** carwatch is a rough-draft demo of one idea: plug it into one car, let it learn
528	that car's normal, and have it say when something acts strange. The claim we defend:
529	
530	> *carwatch learns this CR-V's normal across its Mode 01 engine sensors, flags behavior
531	> outside it, and names the likely fault area. We report how often it catches faults we
532	> induce — a vacuum leak, a cooling restriction, an unplugged sensor — and how often it
533	> false-alarms.*
534	
535	Not "predicts failure." Not "generalizes to any car." Not oil life.
536	
537	**Fault areas (first draft, refined by the M2 design):** cooling; air/fuel mixture
538	(vacuum leak, MAF, O2); sensor or electrical (a dead or unplugged sensor, supply voltage);
539	and "unusual, area unknown" when behavior leaves normal without matching an area. Every
540	area still needs two cooperating sensors to call (D.4).
541	
542	**Why.** Camden, 2026-09-23: the build is one car, one Bluetooth OBD2 adapter and one
543	USB-powered Pi with storage and our model, and the goal is the first attainable step of
544	the idea, not a finished product. D-003 made oil-pressure degradation diagnostic #1, but
545	the CR-V most likely publishes no analog oil pressure (D-007), and trending oil life
546	needed a full oil interval of calendar time. A general monitor uses every sensor the car
547	does publish, and still meets handout §5: a narrow, measured claim.
548	
549	**What changed with it.** Oil is one sensor among many if the CR-V publishes it (PID 0x5C
550	oil temperature), never a headline. Board items `oilq` and `foil` are cut. The analysis
551	pipeline (§D.2), mechanisms D and E, and the two-sensor rule are unchanged.
552	
553	### E.2 — Induced ground truth ⚠️ UNREVIEWED
554	
555	`D-021` (corollary) · **By:** Camden + Claude · **Reviewed:** Camden ⬜ / Lance ⬜
556	· **Supersedes:** the D-003 corollary (§G.5)
557	
558	We cannot wait a semester for a failure, so we provoke one per fault area and label the
559	recordings:
560	
561	- **Air/fuel** — briefly disconnect a small vacuum line. Reversible, safe, moves LTFT
562	  within a minute.
563	- **Cooling** — partially block radiator airflow with cardboard.
564	- **Sensor** — unplug a sensor. Also demo day's injected fault, so it gets rehearsed.
565	
566	Ten labeled recordings we made beat ten thousand unlabeled samples we found, because we
567	know what ours mean — and we will be asked at the defense how we know.
568	
569	### E.3 — 48-hour soak: live sensors vs. a fake OBD2 port ❓ OPEN
570	
571	`D-006` · **Owner:** Camden · **Tracked as:** board item `soakq` (label `decision`)
572	· **Must close before M4** · Blocks nothing before M3
573	
574	**The conflict.** A car cannot run for 48 hours, so Camden's memo (PROBLEM.md, risk)
575	proposes a **fake OBD2 port** that answers Mode 01 requests continuously — board item
576	`obdsim`. Handout §5 endorses exactly this kind of harness as "a legitimate systems
577	artifact." But the same paragraph says: *"The 48-hour soak and the live demonstration run
578	on live sensors; everything else may run on honest replay."* A soak on the fake port is
579	synthesized data by definition, and is labeled `src=synth` everywhere regardless.
580	
581	**Options.**
582	
583	- **(a)** A written exception from Pallickara for a soak on the fake port. The email text
584	  is in the body of board item `soakq`.
585	- **(b)** A sensor on the Pi itself (`pisensor`: MPU-6050 and/or DS18B20, ~$8) runs live
586	  for all 48 hours while the OBD side comes from the fake port, labeled `synth`.
587	- **(c)** The parked CR-V, key in accessory, on the live port with a battery tender. Fully
588	  live, but engine-off values barely move, the socket must stay live in accessory (D-011),
589	  and it ties up Lance's car for two days.
590	
591	**Posture.** Build as if (a) is refused. (b) is the default fallback, which is one more
592	reason `pisensor` is on the critical path. The `src=` field is in the record format
593	regardless.
594	
595	---
596	
597	## F. Process, team and tooling
598	
599	### F.1 — Git and pull-request law 🔒
600	
601	Decided M0 · **By:** Camden · **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜
602	
603	The binding ruleset lives in **`CLAUDE.md` §7**, because that is the file the agent reads
604	every session. Summary of the load-bearing parts:
605	
606	- Claude never commits to `main`, never merges, never force-pushes, never `git add -A`.
607	- One commit = one responsibility, sized by what it is responsible for — not by line
608	  count. *(The original ≤ 150-line / ≤ 3-file and ≤ 500-line PR caps were replaced by the
609	  responsibility test in `CLAUDE.md` §7.3 and §7.5 during M0; CLAUDE.md is the binding
610	  text.)*
611	- One PR = one reviewable claim.
612	- **If the reviewer does not understand a line, the PR does not merge.** The remedy is
613	  explanation or a smaller commit, never trust.
614	- Every commit builds and passes tests on its own.
615	
616	**Why so strict.** Our process grade is computed from transcripts corroborated against
617	commits, the git history is a graded deliverable, and neither of us will break down a
618	thousand-line diff. A commit small enough to review in ninety seconds is a commit we will
619	actually review — and the defense asks us to answer for individual lines.
620	
621	### F.2 — Ownership map 🔒
622	
623	Decided M0 · **By:** Camden · **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜
624	
625	| Owner | Subsystems |
626	| --- | --- |
627	| **Camden** | `src/obd/`, `src/ipc/` |
628	| **Lance** | `src/store/`, `src/analysis/`, `tools/train/` |
629	| **Shared** | `src/supervisor/`, `src/interface/`, `src/common/`, build, docs |
630	
631	Ownership means **first authorship and answerability at the defense**, not exclusivity.
632	Each partner must still be able to answer one question from across the boundary — demo day
633	guarantees one.
634	
635	### F.3 — Milestone dates ⚠️ UNREVIEWED
636	
637	`D-008` · **Owner:** Camden · **Tracked as:** board item `dates` (label `question`)
638	· **Answered:** 2026-09-21, by Camden · **Reviewed:** Camden ⬜ / Lance ⬜
639	
640	**Answer.** Camden verified the milestone dates against the syllabus (checked off in
641	`docs/milestones.md`, 2026-09-21): the milestone dates (now in the `docs/milestones.md`
642	table, D-020) stand as written, M0 2026-09-20 through M6 2026-12-18. Recorded by Claude
643	from that check-off; Camden marks it LOCKED in his own commit.
644	
645	**Why it mattered.** The handout gives weeks, not dates; a one-week error would have moved
646	the M4 soak start, and M4 already lands on Thanksgiving week.
647	
648	### F.4 — Markdown is linted with markdownlint, at a 90-column wrap ⚠️ UNREVIEWED
649	
650	`D-018` · **By:** Claude, in Camden's session 2026-09-23
651	· **Reviewed:** Camden ⬜ / Lance ⬜
652	
653	`.markdownlint.jsonc` at the repository root sets the rules the VS Code markdownlint
654	extension enforces: every default rule on, lines wrapped at **90 columns** (tables, code
655	and headings exempt), `<details>`, `<summary>`, `<code>`, `<sub>` and `<br>` allowed as
656	inline HTML, and tables in the compact `| a | b |` / `| --- | --- |` style.
657	`.markdownlintignore` excludes `docs/handout/`, which is a transcription of the
658	instructor's PDF.
659	
660	Spelling is **American English**, checked by the VS Code Code Spell Checker (cSpell).
661	`cspell.json` holds the project dictionary: our jargon, command names and board slugs.
662	Add a word there when it is a real term; fix it when it is a typo.
663	
664	**Why 90, not the default 80.** The docs were already wrapped at about 90: at 80 the repo
665	raised 1,184 line-length warnings, and at 90 it raised 24. Rewrapping everything to 80
666	would bury every file's history in reflow for no reader benefit.
667	
668	**Why a config at all.** Without one, each editor shows over 1,500 warnings, and a real
669	problem (a broken heading tree, a list that does not render) is invisible in the noise.
670	
671	### F.5 — The milestone checklist is the board; board.toml is retired ⚠️ UNREVIEWED
672	
673	`D-020` · Decided M1, 2026-09-23 · **By:** Camden (in session) + Claude
674	· **Reviewed:** Camden ⬜ / Lance ⬜
675	
676	**Decision.** `docs/milestones.md` is the single source of truth for all work. Every
677	checkbox under a `## M<n>` heading is one GitHub issue, linked by a hidden `<!-- #n -->`
678	tag that `tools/board_sync.py` writes. Tick a box and sync: the issue closes and the card
679	moves to Done. Add a line and sync: a new issue appears. Bold lines are the milestone's
680	exit criteria; plain lines are the tasks under them. `docs/BOARD/board.toml` and
681	`board.lock.json` are retired; every one of their 99 issues became a line, and nothing
682	was closed or deleted to get there.
683	
684	**Why.** Camden's call: 99 items with bodies, dependencies and labels in a TOML file was
685	more board than two people can follow, and it duplicated the exit criteria kept in
686	`milestones.md`. A checklist is what we already read; making it the board removes the
687	second copy.
688	
689	**What changed with it.**
690	
691	- Issue **bodies** are no longer generated. GitHub owns them; the old text stays there.
692	- **Dependencies** (`blocked_by`) and the auto-applied `blocked` label are gone. Order
693	  within a milestone is the plan.
694	- The `--close-questions` flag is gone. Ticking a box is the human act, so **Claude
695	  never ticks a question, decision or hardware line** (CLAUDE.md §7.11).
696	- Milestone due dates are edited in the `milestones.md` table itself.
697	
698	**Cost.** Less structure: no enforced dependency order, and a closed issue explains
699	itself only through its body and comments. If the board grows unwieldy again, the
700	fix is fewer lines, not more tooling.
701	
702	---
703	
704	## G. Superseded
705	
706	When a decision is replaced, it moves here with a pointer to its replacement. Never delete
707	one: the reasoning is evidence, and "what M2 got wrong" is a graded section of
708	`docs/DESIGN.md`.
709	
710	### G.1 — (was A.1) CAN reaches the Pi via MCP2515 on SPI, not Bluetooth 🗑
711	
712	`D-001` · Decided M0 · **By:** Camden + Claude · **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜
713	· **Superseded 2026-09-21 by D-015 (now §G.4)** — raw CAN became a stretch goal.
714	
715	**Decision.** The Pi reads raw CAN frames through an MCP2515 + TJA1050 module on SPI0,
716	with the controller's `INT` line on a GPIO for edge-triggered receive. Not a Bluetooth
717	ELM327 dongle.
718	
719	**Why.** A Bluetooth ELM327 hands us parsed ASCII over a userspace socket at a few
720	samples per second. With no interrupt line, no SPI transaction and no bus-level timing,
721	mechanisms **A, B, C and F all become unavailable** — and the handout requires at least
722	two mechanisms implemented by us, below the application layer. The MCP2515 path keeps
723	the kernel boundary inside our repository, where it is graded. It is also better for the
724	user: raw bus access sees frames the ELM327 protocol never exposes, at the rate the ECU
725	publishes them rather than the rate a request/response dongle can poll.
726	
727	**Cost.** More wiring, a 3.3 V/5 V level question to get right, one-time decode work per
728	vehicle. Accepted.
729	
730	**What replaced it, and what that cost.** D-015 accepts the mechanism loss this entry
731	warned about, in exchange for hardware that works on day one; D-017 records which
732	mechanisms survive. D-019 then moved that adapter to Bluetooth, the option this entry
733	rejected, at no further mechanism cost.
734	
735	### G.2 — (was A.2) Testbeds: Subaru Outback and Lance's Honda 🗑
736	
737	`D-005` · Decided M0 · **By:** Camden · **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜
738	· **Superseded 2026-09-21 by D-016 (§A.2)** — the second vehicle was cut, as this entry
739	said it would be first.
740	
741	**Decision.** Two daily-driven vehicles — Camden's Subaru Outback and Lance's Honda.
742	
743	**Why.** The product's thesis is that a generic maintenance interval is a generalization
744	and your car is not generic. One vehicle cannot demonstrate that; two with different duty
745	cycles can, and the comparison is the demo's strongest five seconds. Two also gives each
746	partner a vehicle they can instrument on their own schedule.
747	
748	**Cost.** Roughly doubles decode and baseline-collection work, and the baseline window is
749	the one thing that cannot be compressed by working harder in Week 14. Mitigation: start
750	on standard Mode 01 PIDs only; manufacturer-specific frames are a stretch.
751	
752	**Risk.** If the schedule slips, the **first** thing cut is the second vehicle — not a
753	mechanism, and not the evaluation. Record it here if it happens.
754	
755	### G.3 — (was B.1) Mechanism commitments: B, D, E, F 🗑
756	
757	`D-002` · Decided M0 · **By:** Camden + Claude · **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜
758	· **Superseded 2026-09-21 by D-017 (§B.1)** — with raw CAN a stretch goal (D-015), B and F
759	lost their data source.
760	
761	The handout requires two. We commit four and will measure all of them.
762	
763	**B — interrupt-driven input with a polling comparison.** `src/can/`. At 500 kbit/s a busy
764	bus delivers a frame roughly every 230 µs; the MCP2515's two receive buffers overflow in
765	milliseconds. A poll loop either burns a core or drops frames. Measured as event-latency
766	distribution and CPU, both ways, idle and loaded.
767	
768	**D — custom append-only storage, crash-consistent.** `src/store/`. *The defining
769	constraint: power is cut mid-write every time the key turns off.* We never get a clean
770	shutdown. Measured by pulling power mid-write, repeatedly, and proving recovery.
771	
772	**E — multi-process with a supervisor.** `src/supervisor/`, `src/ipc/`. A recorder that
773	dies silently has actively harmed its user, who believes it is on duty. Any child may be
774	`kill -9`'d; the system degrades, logs, recovers.
775	
776	**F — no-drop SPSC ring, sequence-accounted.** `src/ipc/ring.c`. Key-on produces a burst;
777	a gap in the record is a gap in the diagnosis. Measured as sustained rate with zero drops
778	under contention.
779	
780	**Stretch, M4+ only:** **A** (character driver for the MCP2515) and **C** (`SCHED_FIFO` on
781	the capture path). Do not start either until B, D, E and F are implemented *and measured*.
782	A half-finished kernel module is worth zero points and costs two weeks.
783	
784	### G.4 — (was A.1) The Pi reads OBD2 through a USB adapter; raw CAN is a stretch goal 🗑
785	
786	`D-015` · Decided M1, 2026-09-21 · **By:** Camden + Claude
787	· **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜
788	· **Supersedes:** D-001 (§G.1)
789	· **Superseded 2026-09-23 by D-019 (§A.1)**: the same protocol over Bluetooth Classic,
790	with this USB adapter kept as the fallback.
791	
792	**Decision.** A USB OBD2 adapter with an ELM327-compatible chip plugs into the OBD2 port
793	and appears on the Pi as a serial device, pinned to `/dev/obd` by a udev rule. Our C daemon
794	sends Mode 01 requests over it and parses the replies. Prefer an STN-chip adapter (e.g.
795	OBDLink SX) over a clone ELM327. No MCP2515, no SPI, no CAN wiring.
796	
797	**Raw CAN is a stretch goal** — an MCP2515 on SPI, taken up only after mechanisms D and E
798	are implemented *and measured*.
799	
800	**Why.** Camden's call (PROMPTLOG E-02): time spent making raw CAN access work was time
801	not spent on the problem. The adapter speaks every OBD2 protocol for us, which is exactly
802	what a plug-in product (D-011) needs, and it removes a class of hardware risk — 5 V on
803	MISO, crystal frequency, bus termination — that could kill a Pi or disturb a daily
804	driver's bus.
805	
806	**Cost — the reason D-001 existed, still true.** An adapter hands us parsed ASCII at
807	roughly 10–20 PID replies per second, with no interrupt line and no bus timing. That
808	takes most of the mechanism menu away from the OBD data path; **D-017** records what
809	survives. Clone ELM327s are also unreliable (truncated buffers, fake firmware), which is
810	why the STN chip is preferred.
811	
812	**Consequences.** The capture daemon becomes a serial reader. Wiring, BOM, provisioning
813	and the design doc follow. The PID survey needs no extra hardware — the same adapter does
814	it.
815	
816	### G.5 — (was E.1) Three induced-and-measured diagnostics, and no more 🗑
817	
818	`D-003` · Decided M0 · **By:** Camden + Claude · **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜
819	· **Superseded 2026-09-23 by D-021 (§E.1)**: reopened by Camden in session; oil life
820	and the fixed three diagnostics gave way to a general monitor with fault areas.
821	
822	The claim we defend is: *"detects the three faults we can induce on this vehicle, with
823	these error rates."* Not "predicts failure." Not "generalizes to any post-1996 car."
824	*(Narrowed from "these two vehicles" by D-016, 2026-09-21.)*
825	
826	1. **Oil pressure degradation across oil life** — residual after normalizing for RPM and
827	   temperature, trended across an interval.
828	2. **Cooling system anomaly** — thermostat short-cycling signature (period and amplitude)
829	   and abnormal warm-up slope, gated on ambient temp and load.
830	3. **Mixture drift** — long-term fuel trim divergence as a function of load.
831	
832	**Why.** Handout §5 says it directly: a narrow claim met and measured outscores a broad
833	claim gestured at. Twelve vague diagnoses is the named failure mode for this project's
834	seed.
835	
836	#### (was E.2) Induced ground truth, D-003 corollary 🗑
837	
838	`D-003` (corollary) · **By:** Camden + Claude · **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜
839	
840	We cannot wait a semester for a failure, so we provoke conditions and label the recordings:
841	
842	- **Vacuum leak** — briefly disconnect a small vacuum line. Reversible, safe, moves LTFT
843	  within a minute.
844	- **Cooling** — partially block radiator airflow with cardboard.
845	- **Sensor fault** — unplug a sensor. Also demo day's injected fault, so it gets rehearsed.
846	- **Oil** — log continuously across a real oil change on the CR-V. Cannot be faked
847	  and cannot be rushed, which is why baseline collection starts at M2.
848	
849	Ten labeled recordings we made beat ten thousand unlabeled samples we found, because we
850	know what ours mean — and we will be asked at the defense how we know.
851	
852	---
853	
854	## Adding a decision
855	
856	Append it to the right category with the next free `D-###` for citation, and fill every
857	field. If Claude made it without a human present, it is ⚠️ **UNREVIEWED** and it goes in the
858	Review Queue at the top — **in the same commit that implements it**, never a later one.
859	
860	**Closing an open question.** When a human answers a `decision` or `question` issue, the
861	answer moves here as a 🔒 LOCKED entry citing the issue number, and the issue closes. One
862	commit does both — resolving one question is one responsibility, however many lines it
863	touches across this file (`CLAUDE.md` §7.3, documentation rules).
864
