# Bill of materials

> **Nothing on this page is ordered until the paper design is signed** (D-024). Then
> order the dongle first: shipping time is the most common silent schedule-killer on this
> project (handout §16).

The product is one box with one USB-C port and one light, plus a Bluetooth OBD2 dongle in
the car's OBD2 port (D-019, D-024). The owner supplies the USB-C charger.

## Core: what we buy

| Qty | Part | ~Cost | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Raspberry Pi 4 (2 GB+) | owned | Both partners already have one. |
| 2 | 32 GB A2 microSD | $20 | A2 endurance matters for a key-cycle soak. Two, because the soak eats cards. |
| 1 | OBDLink LX, Bluetooth Classic OBD2 dongle (STN chip) | ~$60, verify | The data path (D-019). Bluetooth Classic (SPP), **not BLE**. A cheap ELM327 Bluetooth clone is enough for the first PID survey but is unreliable for a 48 h run. |
| 1 | USB-C cable, short, 3 A-rated | $6 | From the owner's charger to the box. |
| — | USB-C car charger | owner's | Not supplied: the box takes whatever the owner has (D-024). It must go dead with the key off (`keyoff`). |
| 1 | USB-C power meter (inline) | $10 | Settles "does this charger go dead at key-off, what does it deliver, and does it sag at crank" in seconds. |

**Fallback, not ordered:** a USB OBD2 adapter with an STN chip (e.g. OBDLink SX, ~$30,
D-015) if Bluetooth proves unreliable in the car.

## The box: designed, not ordered (D-024)

Listed by function. A part number is added only with its datasheet linked and checked by
a human (`CLAUDE.md` §8.4). Sizes marked *estimate* come from the power worksheet
(`powerspec`), not from measurement.

| Qty | Function | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | USB-C receptacle, wired as a sink: 5.1 kΩ on CC1 and CC2 | The only power input. |
| 1 | Input protection: transient suppressor, reverse-polarity protection, fuse | |
| 1 | Input current limit and inrush limiter | Reads the source's CC advertisement (default, 1.5 A or 3 A). |
| 2 | Supercapacitor cells, 2.7 V, about 20 F each (about 10 F in series) | *Estimate.* Needs cell balancing and a fuse; the temperature rating must cover a parked car's cabin. |
| 1 | Power-path controller | The source feeds the Pi first; the bank fills only the gap. |
| 1 | 5 V / 3 A converter that can step up | The bank's voltage falls as it discharges. |
| 1 | Source-present divider and halt-done switch | GPIOs chosen in the schematic (`schpi`). |
| 1 | 5 mm LED + 330 Ω resistor + 2 jumper wires | The warning light (D-014). Any color; pick it for the enclosure. |
| 1 | Heatsink for the Pi | A Pi 4 throttles near 80 °C (`thermal`). |
| 1 | Shell: heat-resistant plastic (ABS, ASA or similar), vent slots, no metal near the antenna | `enclspec`. PLA softens near 60 °C, below a parked cabin's temperature. A food container is an acceptable prototype (handout). |

## Conditional — only if `pisensor` or D-006 resolves to "add physical sensors"

| Qty | Part | ~Cost | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | MPU-6050 IMU | $4 | I2C 400 kHz, hardware FIFO, `INT` pin. The only way mechanisms B and F come back (D-017), and vibration data the ECU cannot see. |
| 1 | DS18B20 waterproof probe | $4 | 1-Wire, kernel driver exists. |
| 1 | 4.7 kΩ resistor | — | 1-Wire pull-up. |

## Stretch — raw CAN (D-019)

Not ordered unless the stretch goal is taken up after mechanisms D and E are measured.

| Qty | Part | ~Cost | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | MCP2515 + TJA1050 CAN module | $8 | Check the crystal (8 vs 16 MHz) and meter MISO for 5 V before it touches the Pi. |
| 1 | OBD2 pass-through Y-splitter | $10 | Pins 6, 14, 5. |
| 1 | Logic analyzer (8ch clone) | $12 | Settles SPI timing arguments. |

# Wiring and electrical safety

The product is one box with one USB-C port and one light, plus a Bluetooth OBD2 dongle
in the car's OBD2 port (D-019, D-024). Nothing on the car is cut, spliced or pierced.

```text
  OBD2 port ──[Bluetooth OBD2 dongle]~~ RFCOMM ~~▶ Pi (/dev/rfcomm0 → /dev/obd)

  owner's USB-C charger ──USB-C──▶ [box: power block, supercapacitor] ──5 V──▶ Pi
                                        │  source-present (divided to 3.3 V) ──▶ GPIO
                                        ◀── halt-done ─────────────────────── GPIO
  Pi GPIO17 ──330 Ω──▶ LED ──▶ GND          (warning light)
```

GPIO numbers for source-present and halt-done are set in the schematic (`schpi`), not
here.

> **The Pi's GPIO is 3.3 V and has zero over-voltage protection.** Source-present comes
> from the 5 V USB input, so it reaches the header only through a divider; meter it
> before it is connected. Wire everything with the Pi powered off.

## OBD2 dongle → Pi (D-019)

| Item | Value | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dongle | OBDLink LX (STN chip) | **Bluetooth Classic, Serial Port Profile. Not BLE:** a BLE-only adapter has no RFCOMM channel and will not bind. |
| Connection | The Pi's built-in Bluetooth | Paired and trusted once with `bluetoothctl`; record the dongle's MAC address here. |
| Stable name | `/dev/obd` | `rfcomm bind 0 <MAC> 1` creates `/dev/rfcomm0` at every boot, and a udev rule links it to `/dev/obd` (`scripts/provision_pi.sh`). The daemon never opens an `rfcomm` number. |
| Baud | ignored | RFCOMM carries bytes without a line rate; `screen` and `obdd` may set any baud. |
| Fallback | USB OBD2 adapter (D-015, §G.4) | Swap the udev rule to match its vendor/product ID; nothing else changes. |
| Protocol | `ATSP0` (automatic) | The dongle negotiates the car's OBD2 protocol itself. Record what it chose (`ATDP`) in `pid-survey.md`. |
| Dongle power | OBD2 pin 16 — **live with the key off** | The dongle draws from the car even when parked. Measure its key-off current (board item `dongledrain`) before leaving it plugged in overnight. |

## Power — the box's USB-C input (D-024)

The box takes the owner's own USB-C charger. Its power block (requirements in
`docs/DECISIONS.md` §A.6):

1. sinks 5 V only (5.1 kΩ on both CC pins), behind transient and reverse-polarity
   protection and a fuse;
2. limits input current below what the source advertises, and limits inrush into the
   empty supercapacitor bank;
3. feeds the Pi from the source first and from the bank only for the gap;
4. reports source-present on a GPIO;
5. cuts the Pi's supply when the Pi signals halt-done, even if the source has returned,
   then re-enables after a short off time;
6. powers on again by itself when the source returns.

**Not supported:** a charger that stays live with the key off. The box would stay on.

An undervolted Pi keeps running and corrupts the SD card later. Prove the supply; do not
trust its label.

### Measurements (dated; a row without a result has not been done)

| Measurement | How | Feeds | Date | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Does the owner's charger go dead with the key off? Is it live in accessory? | USB-C meter, key off / ACC / run | `keyoff` | | |
| Supply dip at crank | meter or scope at the charger's output | `cranklog`, the grace period | | |
| Pi 4 draw by state: boot, idle, loaded, shutdown | USB-C meter | `powerspec` | | |
| Boot time and shutdown time on the real image | `systemd-analyze`, log timestamps | `bootbudget` | | |
| Bank discharge into a dummy load; charge time from empty | meter, stopwatch | `capbench` | | |
| `vcgencmd get_throttled` after a cold start | on the Pi; must be `0x0` | `keyoff` | | |
| Pi and bank temperature in a sealed shell, hot cabin | Pi sensor, thermometer | `thermal` | | |
| Dongle key-off current from pin 16 | meter | `dongledrain` | | |

## Warning light → Pi (D-014)

| Part | Pi pin | Pi signal | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| LED anode, via 330 Ω | 11 | GPIO17 (proposed) | ~4 mA at 3.3 V — well inside the pin's limit. Written only by the supervisor. |
| LED cathode | 9 | GND | |

Every live state is a blink pattern; a **steady** light, on or off, means the device is not
running (DECISIONS §B.5).

## Bring-up order

1. Pi on the bench, dongle powered, no car: `bluetoothctl` pairs and trusts it, then
   `rfcomm bind 0 <MAC> 1`, `ls -l /dev/obd`, and `ATZ` answers with the dongle's
   version string. Reboot once and confirm `/dev/obd` comes back without a hand.
2. Car, key to run, engine off: `0100` returns the supported-PID bitmap.
3. Car, engine running: `010C` (RPM) changes when you touch the throttle.
4. The power measurements above: the free ones first (the owner's charger with a meter,
   key off and at crank), the bank only after the power design is signed.

Measured results go in this file, dated. A step without a recorded result has not been
done (CLAUDE.md §8.4).

```text
                                        ◀── halt-done ─────────────────────── GPIO
  Pi GPIO17 ──330 Ω──▶ LED ──▶ GND          (warning light)
```

GPIO numbers for source-present and halt-done are set in the schematic (`schpi`), not
here.

> **The Pi's GPIO is 3.3 V and has zero over-voltage protection.** Source-present comes
> from the 5 V USB input, so it reaches the header only through a divider; meter it
> before it is connected. Wire everything with the Pi powered off.

## OBD2 dongle → Pi (D-019)

| Item | Value | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dongle | OBDLink LX (STN chip) | **Bluetooth Classic, Serial Port Profile. Not BLE:** a BLE-only adapter has no RFCOMM channel and will not bind. |
| Connection | The Pi's built-in Bluetooth | Paired and trusted once with `bluetoothctl`; record the dongle's MAC address here. |
| Stable name | `/dev/obd` | `rfcomm bind 0 <MAC> 1` creates `/dev/rfcomm0` at every boot, and a udev rule links it to `/dev/obd` (`scripts/provision_pi.sh`). The daemon never opens an `rfcomm` number. |
| Baud | ignored | RFCOMM carries bytes without a line rate; `screen` and `obdd` may set any baud. |
| Fallback | USB OBD2 adapter (D-015, §G.4) | Swap the udev rule to match its vendor/product ID; nothing else changes. |
| Protocol | `ATSP0` (automatic) | The dongle negotiates the car's OBD2 protocol itself. Record what it chose (`ATDP`) in `pid-survey.md`. |
| Dongle power | OBD2 pin 16 — **live with the key off** | The dongle draws from the car even when parked. Measure its key-off current (board item `dongledrain`) before leaving it plugged in overnight. |

## Power — the box's USB-C input (D-024)

The box takes the owner's own USB-C charger. Its power block (requirements in
`docs/DECISIONS.md` §A.6):

1. sinks 5 V only (5.1 kΩ on both CC pins), behind transient and reverse-polarity
   protection and a fuse;
2. limits input current below what the source advertises, and limits inrush into the
   empty supercapacitor bank;
3. feeds the Pi from the source first and from the bank only for the gap;
4. reports source-present on a GPIO;
5. cuts the Pi's supply when the Pi signals halt-done, even if the source has returned,
   then re-enables after a short off time;
6. powers on again by itself when the source returns.

**Not supported:** a charger that stays live with the key off. The box would stay on.

An undervolted Pi keeps running and corrupts the SD card later. Prove the supply; do not
trust its label.

### Measurements (dated; a row without a result has not been done)

| Measurement | How | Feeds | Date | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Does the owner's charger go dead with the key off? Is it live in accessory? | USB-C meter, key off / ACC / run | `keyoff` | | |
| Supply dip at crank | meter or scope at the charger's output | `cranklog`, the grace period | | |
| Pi 4 draw by state: boot, idle, loaded, shutdown | USB-C meter | `powerspec` | | |
| Boot time and shutdown time on the real image | `systemd-analyze`, log timestamps | `bootbudget` | | |
| Bank discharge into a dummy load; charge time from empty | meter, stopwatch | `capbench` | | |
| `vcgencmd get_throttled` after a cold start | on the Pi; must be `0x0` | `keyoff` | | |
| Pi and bank temperature in a sealed shell, hot cabin | Pi sensor, thermometer | `thermal` | | |
| Dongle key-off current from pin 16 | meter | `dongledrain` | | |

## Warning light → Pi (D-014)

| Part | Pi pin | Pi signal | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| LED anode, via 330 Ω | 11 | GPIO17 (proposed) | ~4 mA at 3.3 V — well inside the pin's limit. Written only by the supervisor. |
| LED cathode | 9 | GND | |

Every live state is a blink pattern; a **steady** light, on or off, means the device is not
running (DECISIONS §B.5).

## Bring-up order

1. Pi on the bench, dongle powered, no car: `bluetoothctl` pairs and trusts it, then
   `rfcomm bind 0 <MAC> 1`, `ls -l /dev/obd`, and `ATZ` answers with the dongle's
   version string. Reboot once and confirm `/dev/obd` comes back without a hand.
2. Car, key to run, engine off: `0100` returns the supported-PID bitmap.
3. Car, engine running: `010C` (RPM) changes when you touch the throttle.
4. The power measurements above: the free ones first (the owner's charger with a meter,
   key off and at crank), the bank only after the power design is signed.

Measured results go in this file, dated. A step without a recorded result has not been
done (CLAUDE.md §8.4).

        is labeled an estimate. Nothing is ordered.

`D-027` · Decided M2, 2026-10-21 · **By:** Camden (in session) + Claude
· **Reviewed:** Camden ⬜ / Lance ⬜
· **Supersedes:** D-014 (§G.10)

**Decision.** One LED, visible through the shell, shows red, yellow or green. It is
written **only by the supervisor** (D-014's rule, kept).

| Light | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| green, slow pulse (about 1 Hz) | Ready: booted, recording, all systems go |
| yellow, medium blink (about 2 Hz) | Running on stored energy: riding a supply dip, or shutting down |
| red, fast blink (about 4 Hz) | An issue, in the box **or** in the car; the report says which |
| steady yellow | Booting: held on from power-up, before the supervisor runs |
| any other steady light, or dark while the car runs | **Not running.** Never a valid live state |
| dark while the car is off | Normal: the box is off |

Priority when more than one applies: red over yellow over green. Steady yellow for more
than about a minute means the boot never finished.

**What counts as red.** In the box: a child down or restart-limited; the dongle silent
while the engine runs; storage failing or nearly full; undervoltage or thermal
throttling; the supercapacitor's self-check failed. In the car: a verdict has surfaced
after hysteresis and dwell (D.3), or a sensor the car stopped answering.

**Why every live state pulses.** D-014's reasoning, applied to three colors: a GPIO keeps
its last level after the process driving it dies, so a steady green would freeze into a
false all-clear if the supervisor crashed. If every live state blinks, a frozen light of
any color can only mean "not running". Camden asked for whichever pattern is safer (P11),
and this is.

**The boot state.** The Pi spends roughly half a minute (estimate, `bootbudget`) booting
before any software can drive the light. Yellow is held on from power-up in hardware: a
pull keeps it lit while its GPIO is still an input, and once the supervisor drives the
pin, the pin wins. Camden's choice (R4). The firmware's `gpio=` setting in `config.txt`
might do the same with no parts; confirm on the board before relying on it.

**The part.** Whether yellow is its own die or red and green mixed is a part choice (two
GPIOs or three), made in `ledspec` from the LED's datasheet, which also sets the
resistors. Pins are assigned in the schematic (`schpi`).

**Why.** Camden, 2026-10-21 (`docs/REVISION_PLAN.md` §1.1, P10, P11): one light, three
colors, and red means an issue in either the box or the car.

**Cost.** Two or three GPIOs instead of one; the supervisor's blink timer still must never
delay `waitpid` handling; the colors must stay distinguishable through the shell
(`enclspec`). Red merges box and car issues, so the report must say which.

**Alternative rejected.** D-014's single-color patterns (a double-blink for a verdict): a
pattern code the owner has to learn.

a = "| D-024 | One box"; i = s.index(a); j = s.index("\n", i)+1
s = s[:j] + "| D-027 | One tri-color status light; every live state pulses; steady yellow while booting (§B.5, supersedes D-014) | Camden (in session) + Claude | 2026-10-21 | Both — it is the one output a driver sees |\n" + s[j:]

 ("""GPIO numbers for source-present and halt-done are set in the schematic (`schpi`), not

 ("""## Warning light → Pi (D-014)

  "- [ ] M3 supervisor: drive the tri-color light from child health, verdicts and power\n      events `led` <!-- #89 -->"),

  "- [ ] M2 docs: power-event state machine and the grace period `shutfsm`\n- [ ] M2 docs: tri-color light patterns, priority, the boot state and the LED part\n      `ledspec`\n"),
])
EOF

one button: **Download report**. The report is one self-contained HTML file plus a CSV of
the same data, generated on the box by a C program in `src/interface/`. The page still
writes nothing to the device. A native phone app is a stretch goal, not planned for M2 to
M5.

**Report contents** (first draft; finalized in `reportspec`):

| Section | Content |
| --- | --- |
| Header | Box id, report time, whether wall-clock time is trustworthy, and the mix of data sources (`live`, `replay`, `synth`), always labeled (C.2) |
| Sessions | Each key cycle: boot id, start, end, duration, ended cleanly or recovered, records lost on recovery |
| Box health | Process liveness and restarts, ring overruns (must be zero), undervoltage and throttle events, temperature, the supercapacitor's self-check, free storage |
| Car findings | Each surfaced verdict: fault area, the sensors that cooperated to call it, residual and trend evidence, when it began and ended, confidence |
| Baseline maturity | Hours of normal driving learned per operating-point bin, so the owner knows how far to trust the verdicts |
| Absent signals | Any PID the car stopped answering, and for how long |

**Reachability.** The box is off whenever the car is (D-024), so a phone reaches it only
while the car runs, or while the box is plugged into any USB-C charger at home, where it
boots and serves the same page.

trends on a phone and downloads a report that says what is wrong with the box or the car.
HTML opens on any phone with no app, and the CSV lets the owner or a mechanic take the
numbers elsewhere. C, as D-013 recommended: the server is small, and an interpreter would
add tens of megabytes to the 48-hour memory plot (R3).

`obdctl` uses, so every number in it can also be produced at the CLI, and every graded
behavior stays demonstrable through `obdctl` alone.

table, its memory shows in the soak plot, and the boundary check still has to show the
page is the only network code.

**Alternatives rejected.** A PDF report (needs a PDF writer we would have to defend). A
native app (a second product to build). A Python server in `ui/` (the soak's memory).

    p = pathlib.Path(path); s = p.read_text()

reps = [
 ("""---

## B. Systems architecture and mechanisms""",
  """### A.8 — A real-time clock keeps wall time while the box is off ⚠️ UNREVIEWED

`D-030` · Decided M2, 2026-10-21 · **By:** Camden (in session) + Claude
· **Reviewed:** Camden ⬜ / Lance ⬜

**Decision.** The box gets a small real-time clock module on the Pi's I2C bus, kept
running by its own backup cell or capacitor while the box is off. At boot the system
clock is set from it. If the clock reports its time as invalid (its backup was lost),
that session's wall time is marked untrusted. Every record still carries `mono_ns`
regardless. The phone page stays read-only: it does not set the clock.

**Why.** The Pi has no battery-backed clock, and the box has no network (`CLAUDE.md`
§2.3). Raspberry Pi OS's `fake-hwclock` restores the time saved at the last shutdown, so
the clock does not advance while the box is off, and every boot would appear to follow the
previous shutdown directly. The soak (D-023) must prove a 48-hour wall-clock span across
parked gaps, and the report's session list needs real times. Camden chose the clock
module, 2026-10-21, over the phone setting the time (that depends on someone opening the
page on every drive) and over no wall clock at all (`docs/REVISION_PLAN.md` §1.2, R5).

**Cost.**

- One more part, on I2C (GPIO2 and GPIO3, header pins 3 and 5), drawn in the Pi interface
  block, and bought only after the design is signed.
- Its backup cell or capacitor lives in a parked car's cabin, so its temperature rating
  must cover that, checked against the part's datasheet (`rtcspec`).
- A clock that has drifted or lost its backup must be detected rather than trusted, so the
  boot path checks it (`rtcboot`).

---

## B. Systems architecture and mechanisms"""),

- **Transactions (`storaged`).** `storaged` drains the ring into batches: a
  `BEGIN(txn_id)` record, the sample records, a `COMMIT(txn_id)` record, then one

  each CRC'd and carrying a generation counter, so a checkpoint torn by a power cut never
  destroys the previous good one.

  committed, verifying every CRC. The scan stops at the first bad record and truncates the
  torn tail, and a batch with no `COMMIT` is truncated at its `BEGIN` (**undo**).

  batch after its offset (**redo**), through the same code as live analysis. Both log
  exactly what was recovered and what was lost, as counts and offsets.

  ended in a clean shutdown or was recovered.

the defense, and do not claim an undo log the design does not need.

pointer.

content.text:
The review's findings mostly hold up, so I'll fix them before publishing. What I accept, grouped by commit:

- **D-031:** `analyzed` must read only up to an offset `storaged` publishes after `fsync` returns, or a page-cache read can absorb a batch a power cut erases. I also accept that it's unstated how verdicts and events reach durable storage.
- **D-024:** a seconds-scale bank can't "supplement" a source that is weak for a whole drive. Reading the CC advertisement needs a detector part, since the Pi has no ADC. The energy budget leaves out the grace period. An always-live charger would drain the car battery.
- **`expcrash`:** pulling the charger now triggers a clean shutdown, so crash trials must cut the Pi's own rail.
- **D-025:** needs a clean-shutdown record kind, or a crash right after a commit looks like a clean end.
- **D-027:** the light between the supervisor starting and its children's first heartbeats is undefined.
- **Rubric gaps:** mechanism E's "sensors in separate processes", a live car needed on demo day, and few powered hours in the soak window.
- **Leftover stale wording:** "always-on", "open work has owners", "per diagnostic".

I'm not taking its board-rewording suggestion: cutting lines is your tick. Its BOM-versus-`order` point is not a contradiction, because both say nothing is bought until the plan is signed.

**Project:** `carwatch`, an always-on in-vehicle diagnostic recorder that learns *this*
**This file holds what is DECIDED. Open work and open questions live on the GitHub
board** as issues with owners, milestones and blocked-by dependencies (`CLAUDE.md` §7.11).
An ❓ OPEN entry below exists only as a pointer to its issue, so the reasoning sits beside
| ❓ **OPEN** | Not decided. Blocking something. Owner named. |

`docs/DECISIONS.md` keeps only what has been **decided** (plus the review queue).
Everything still open lives on the board, where it has an owner, a milestone, and a
visible position in the queue.

docs/DESIGN.md:153:| Detection: TPR / FPR per diagnostic | induced-fault fixtures | |
docs/DESIGN.md:154:| Recovery after mid-write power cut | N pull-the-plug trials | 100% |
docs/milestones.md:224:- [ ] M4 experiment: crash consistency — N power-cut trials `expcrash` <!-- #60 -->
| State | Entered when | The supervisor does | Light |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

The review's findings mostly hold up, so I'll fix them before publishing. What I accept, grouped by commit:

- **D-031:** `analyzed` must read only up to an offset `storaged` publishes after `fsync` returns, or a page-cache read can absorb a batch a power cut erases. I also accept that it's unstated how verdicts and events reach durable storage.
- **D-024:** a seconds-scale bank can't "supplement" a source that is weak for a whole drive. Reading the CC advertisement needs a detector part, since the Pi has no ADC. The energy budget leaves out the grace period. An always-live charger would drain the car battery.
- **`expcrash`:** pulling the charger now triggers a clean shutdown, so crash trials must cut the Pi's own rail.
- **D-025:** needs a clean-shutdown record kind, or a crash right after a commit looks like a clean end.
- **D-027:** the light between the supervisor starting and its children's first heartbeats is undefined.
- **Rubric gaps:** mechanism E's "sensors in separate processes", a live car needed on demo day, and few powered hours in the soak window.
- **Leftover stale wording:** "always-on", "open work has owners", "per diagnostic".

I'm not taking its board-rewording suggestion: cutting lines is your tick. Its BOM-versus-`order` point is not a contradiction, because both say nothing is bought until the plan is signed.

`D-031` · Decided M2, 2026-10-21 · **By:** Camden (in session) + Claude
· **Reviewed:** Camden ⬜ / Lance ⬜
· **Fixes:** `docs/DESIGN.md` §1, which fanned one single-consumer ring out to three
readers

**Decision.** The shared-memory SPSC ring has exactly one producer, `obdd`, and one
consumer, `storaged`. `analyzed` does not read the ring: it reads `storaged`'s log, in
order, and only records whose batch has been committed to disk. `obdctl` and the status
page never read samples themselves; they ask the supervisor over its Unix socket, and the
supervisor asks the process that holds the answer.

I've finished stage 1 of the revision plan on `camden/m2/revision-plan`. The redesign is recorded as decisions D-022 to D-031 (all ⚠️ UNREVIEWED), and the branch is pushed with a draft PR: https://github.com/CamdenThomas/CS370-Term-Project/pull/154 (closes #132). `make`, `make test` and `make asan` all pass on the final commit, the full output is pasted in the PR, and markdownlint and cspell are clean on every touched file. I ran the linters through `npx`, which needs no global install.

**Decisions added** (old versions move to §G, never deleted):

| ID | Decision |
| --- | --- |
| D-022 | Your Forester and Lance's CR-V are both testbeds, neither required of anyone; PROBLEM.md keeps Lance as the named user |
| D-023 | The soak is 48 hours wall-clock of normal driving across key cycles, pending the professor's written confirmation |
| D-024 | One box, one USB-C input from the owner's charger, a seconds-scale supercapacitor, off at rest |
| D-025 | Write-ahead transactions and A/B checkpoints; extends 🔒 C.1 with your yes |
| D-026 | No pre-assigned owners; a subsystem belongs to its first substantive commit; replaces 🔒 F.2 with your yes |
| D-027 | One tri-color light, every live state pulses, steady yellow while booting |
| D-028 | The phone page downloads an HTML + CSV report, served by C |
| D-029 | `pisensor` declined; mechanisms D and E are the committed pair |
| D-030 | A real-time clock, because without one the logs can't prove the 48-hour window |
| D-031 | One ring from `obdd` to `storaged`; `analyzed` reads only committed records from the log |

A fresh-context review of the branch found 12 problems, and the real ones are fixed in commits 21–27. The most serious: `analyzed` could have learned from a batch that a power cut then erased. Also: pulling the charger no longer tests crash recovery, because it now triggers a clean shutdown. The supercapacitor's energy margin is thin. An always-live charger would drain the car battery. Demo day needs a running car.
